commits.message:
[iris] Route 02a sandboxes through the CPU gVisor handler (#11345)

Route cw-us-east-02a sandbox Pods through a Pulumi-owned
`iris-gvisor-cpu` RuntimeClass. Kubernetes clusters can select a sandbox
RuntimeClass; the default remains `gvisor`. The 02a class requests
CoreWeave's direct `cw-gvisor-cpu` handler and selects only `cpu-genoa`
nodes labelled for gVisor and that handler. The controller checks that
its configured class exists at startup.

The default `gvisor` path failed during sandbox creation on both H100
and CPU nodes ([incidents 631](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/631) and
[976](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/976)); the node failure remains
undiagnosed. A direct-handler control Pod started on cw-us-west-04a, but
the handler has not been verified on 02a. CoreWeave must enable it on
the 02a CPU nodes. Without its node label, sandbox Pods remain
unschedulable.

Apply the Pulumi-owned RuntimeClass read rule to every CoreWeave stack
before deploying this controller revision. On 02a, apply the CPU
topology resources from
[#11515](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11515) before the
targeted RuntimeClass and RBAC update. The rollout guide in
`lib/iris/OPS.md` then requires a public-image canary on each of the
four eligible CPU nodes, an Iris storage-limit overflow probe, a
capacity check at expected Taskforge concurrency, and a full-pool
`cw-tas` spill canary before normal 02a sandbox traffic resumes.

Part of #10090
Part of #11343

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[datakit] Add a calibrated document low-value scorer (#11500)

Add a CPU structural scorer for low-value documents, with bounded
head/middle/tail reads from replay token caches and a co-partitioned
Datakit quality side leaf. Pin model, calibration and tokenizer bytes;
inference uses a NumPy tree head and the existing tokenizer stack. The
model card records the rubric, artifacts, digests and operating points.

On 891 conclusively labeled frozen test documents (204 low-value, 687
natural), the cutoff calibrated for 5% natural false-drop catches
101/204=49.5% while dropping 18/687=2.62% natural documents (Wilson 95%
interval 1.66–4.10%). The recommended cutoff is `score >=
0.4220386490525259`; the conservative cutoff
`>= 0.5949392992426772` catches 34.8% at 1.16% false-drop (0.59–2.28%).
Calibration targets and actual test rates differ:

| Scorer | Recall, 2% calibration target | Actual false-drop | Recall,
5% calibration target | Actual false-drop |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Structural GBDT | 34.8% | 1.16% | 49.5% | 2.62% |
| Native rules | 13.7% | 0.15% | 18.1% | 2.91% |
| Total-share rules | 15.2% | 0.29% | 17.6% | 2.77% |
| Junkgate2 | 3.4% | 1.75% | 10.8% | 5.68% |

At the 5% point, the paired recall gain is +38.73 percentage points over
junkgate2 (bootstrap 95% 31.37–46.57) and +31.37 over native rules
(24.02–38.73). Native rules preserve the original machine-junk priority;
that additional baseline was evaluated after the first test opening
without changing the learned model or cutoffs.

The 3,600-document sample spans 388 frozen cluster/quality/length
caches. Exact visible-content groups were split before annotation: 2,038
training, 655 calibration and 907 test rows, with 2,009/643/891
conclusive labels. GLM-5.3-Flash labels used durable no-replay receipts;
300 blinded independent Astra labels yielded 93.81% binary agreement on
291 conclusive pairs, and 60 disagreement/tokenizer-marker cases were
adjudicated. Labels are model-assisted judgments. Raw document text and
rationales remain private.

The selected parameters and cutoffs were frozen in [research commit
90d61498a6](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/90d61498a6/logbooks/52-replay-quality-classifier/selected)
before test evaluation. Structural and Harrier-fusion heads tied
validation recall, so the predeclared cost rule selected structural.
Packaging later bound the exact replay tokenizer; its two renamed
tool-call IDs occur in no sampled view, leaving features, labels,
parameters and cutoffs unchanged.

[Public evaluation, PR curves and non-text label
manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/b710b9236d/logbooks/52-replay-quality-classifier/results)
accompany the versioned bundle at
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/models/quality/replay_low_value_v1/2026.11.15.2/`
([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fdatakit%2Fmodels%2Fquality%2Freplay_low_value_v1%2F2026.11.15.2%2F)),
mirrored at the same relative path in east-08a. Model SHA256 is
`1396ad6cdaa9b7d1d9b5c0b2cabde124c4e3fe0e8c869da55e2e2b72bc7f545d`;
calibration SHA256 is
`e650d4e9b71cc55a7feb8d54272d50a195f35a10e8894d9fea4fed119ee41c83`. All
manifest-listed files were verified in both regions.

Seven behavior tests, the affected safe-test runner and strict
documentation build pass. A 100-row actual-cache pilot with eight
workstation threads took 2.90 seconds and matched reference scores
within 2.22e-16; this is not a fleet estimate. Rates describe the
stratified sample, not corpus prevalence or downstream training
improvement. Full replay materialization and Exp3 adoption are separate
pending work.

Based on the replay review in #11188.

Research logbook:
https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/52

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[rl] Let the Snowball quick loop use InfiniBand for NCCL (#11178)

Stop forcing NCCL onto TCP sockets in the Snowball quick-loop recipe.
SkyRL forwards `NCCL_NET`, `NCCL_IB_DISABLE` and `NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY`
into every Ray actor, so the settings added in #10562 put the
trainer-to-vLLM weight sync on TCP. They probably put Megatron's
inter-node collectives on TCP too; that has not been measured.

Timings on the 5-node Snowball layout (4×8 H100 Megatron policy, 1×8
H100 vLLM engine, `expert_block` transport) on cw-us-east-02a:

| Run | Network | Weight sync | Step (median) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Quick loop, five 25-step runs (e.g.
[lvkmgmxm](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin-snowball-curriculum/runs/lvkmgmxm))
| TCP | 6.9–9.1 s | 80–216 s |
| Short-context `maxrl-skyrl-comparison` launcher (not in the repo),
[o38jsojx](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin-snowball-curriculum/runs/o38jsojx),
225 steps | TCP | 7.1 s | 28.6 s |
| `async_rl.py` smoke,
[2t8k34cn](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin-async-rl/runs/2t8k34cn),
2 updates | InfiniBand | 0.50–0.54 s | not comparable |

- Weight sync is serial in the step at staleness 0. Removing ~7 s of
sync would shorten quick-loop steps by about 4–9% and o38jsojx-style
steps by about 23% (projection; sync saving only).
- The smoke ran `experiments/post_training/async_rl.py`, which sets no
NCCL network variables. Its expert phase moved the ~131 GB of
routed-expert weights measured in MarinSkyRL#698 in 0.35 s. The engines
resumed generation after each sync, and the run completed its checkpoint
and Hugging Face export. MarinSkyRL#698 measured 0.56 s for the same
layout over InfiniBand in September.
- The expert phase of every `expert_block` run in
`marin-snowball-curriculum` since 2026-10-20 takes about 6 s or more,
consistent with TCP.

The override was a workaround for an InfiniBand fault:

- On 2026-10-20 both attempts of the first quick-loop smoke on
cw-us-east-02a, run with default NCCL settings, failed at the first
inter-node Megatron collective during model load. Workers on at least
three node pairs, on both `mlx5_0` and `mlx5_1`, logged `NET/IB: Got
completion ... status=IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR(12)` followed by
`ncclRemoteError`. The retry landed on the same nodes and failed the
same way.
- The next smoke forced sockets and passed model load and weight sync.
It and two later smokes failed for unrelated reasons; the fourth
completed. Neither #10562 nor its review records the reason for the
override.
- The smoke above ran on different 02a nodes from those that failed on
2026-10-20, so it shows InfiniBand works on part of the cluster, not
that the fault is gone. If it recurs, the job fails within minutes at
model load, and a retry on the same nodes does not recover. Setting
`NCCL_NET=Socket` and `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` restores the TCP path.

#11069 deletes this launcher, and `snowball_rl.py` on its base branch
sets the same three variables unconditionally, so the same change is
needed there. Before this is marked ready, a matched A/B should measure
the actual step time and record which nodes each arm ran on.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[infra] Check vendored uv locks in pre-commit (#11423)

Makes `./infra/pre-commit.py` catch stale SkyRL and Harbor lockfiles
before a PR is pushed, instead of leaving them to fail CI.

SkyRL (`vendor/skyrl`) and Harbor (`vendor/harbor`) each keep their own
`uv.lock`, and both install Marin libraries from local paths (finelog,
finestore, iris, rigging, rolloutengine, shellbox, skyrlrecipe,
taskcompendium, verifyit). A dependency change in one of those libraries
therefore makes the vendored locks stale, but nothing checked them
before CI. In the week of Nov 6-13, 87 `skyrl-wheel` and `harbor-unit`
jobs failed their lock check, across 68 PR heads:

| What the failing PR head changed | PR heads |
|---|---|
| A library's `pyproject.toml` and the root `uv.lock`, but no vendored
lock | 42 |
| A library's `pyproject.toml` and a vendored lock that was still stale
| 2 |
| A library's `pyproject.toml` and no lock | 1 |
| No dependency file (a stale lock inherited from `main`) | 23 |

The 23 inherited failures came from stale locks reaching `main` itself;
for example, `skyrl-wheel` failed its lock check on `main` on Nov 8.

pre-commit now runs `uv lock --project <vendored project> --check`, the
same command CI runs, when a vendored project's `pyproject.toml` or the
`pyproject.toml` of a library it installs from a local path changes.
Vendored projects are found from `vendor/*/uv.lock`, and each project's
input files are read from its `[tool.uv.sources]`, so both follow future
changes. With `--fix`, the check relocks the stale project and still
reports failure, so the new lock gets staged.

Checked locally with uv 0.13.5: the check passes on `main`, fails for
both projects after adding a dependency to
`lib/shellbox/pyproject.toml`, relocks both under `--fix`, and passes
after the relock. SkyRL requires uv 0.13.5 or newer; with an older uv
the check reports uv's own version error. The lint workflow runs
pre-commit on all files, so this adds about 20 s, mostly SkyRL's
resolution, to each lint run.

---------

Co-authored-by: Amy Sartran <users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[eval] Add typed eval policy declarations and their resolution (#11388)

🤖 Add `experiments/evaluation/policy`, a typed description of one eval
policy version. `resolve(policy, candidate)` combines it into one
`ResolvedPolicyEvaluation` for each evaluation the candidate runs,
holding the context, output limit and seed to run with.

| Policy type | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `PolicyCandidate` | a model catalog `ModelConfig` and the model's
native window (`max_context`) |
| `PolicyEvaluation` | a launcher `EvaluationDefinition`
(`EvaluationSelection` or `HarborDefinition`) and its context, output
limit and seed |
| `PolicyExclusion`, `PolicyOverride` | one candidate's exception on one
evaluation, with a reason |

The policy currently lives in #10197,
`lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/eval_policy.py` (the September cohorts)
and the October campaign's shell scripts and `campaign.yaml` under
`experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/`. These
types are the first step toward one source that both launches and checks
policy runs. They reuse the model catalog and the launcher's evaluation
definitions, and add only what those lack.

Each evaluation states its own settings; there are no policy-wide
defaults. An override replaces the evaluation's context or output limit
for one candidate. A context larger than the candidate's window, or an
output limit that does not fit the context, is an error until the policy
adds an override, so every candidate that runs an evaluation under
different settings is listed in the policy with a reason. A selection
may not set `max_tokens` or `seed` in its run overrides, because the
policy owns them. Exceptions must match a candidate and evaluation in
the policy by value, so an exception built from a stale copy is
rejected.

The window is separate from `serve.max_model_len`, which is the length a
catalog entry serves the model at and is often set below the window to
save memory. It stays out of `ModelConfig` because run records store the
whole `ModelConfig`, and EvalDash groups runs by its digest. The package
lives in `experiments/` because `HarborDefinition` does; it can move
into `lib/marin` once `EvaluationSelection` is the only definition type.

Nothing uses the package yet. Runtime adapters, the October policy and a
`policy` launch command follow in later PRs.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[iris] Keep federation sync loops alive when a handoff fails (#11399)

On 2026-11-13, the `marin` hub's federation-sync threads for
cw-us-east-02a and cw-us-east-08a both exited: 02a at 18:05 UTC and 08a
at 18:53 UTC. The hub stopped delivering jobs to either peer. Each peer
still looked reachable, because its heartbeat thread was still running.
By 20:36 UTC, 112 live jobs were waiting for 02a.

Two faults combined to cause this.

- The hub controller reads every handoff's bundle from its state bucket,
`gs://marin-us-central2`, but the controller runs in us-central1. Each
read counted against rigging's process-wide 10 GB cross-region budget,
which never resets. After about 10.75 days of uptime, the next bundle
read raised `TransferBudgetExceeded`. `BundleStore` now opens its
storage with a new `unbudgeted_url_to_fs`. The store holds job payloads
the controller wrote itself: workspace bundles (capped at 25 MB by
`MAX_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES`) and externalized workdir files (not capped; the
largest since the last rollout is 42 MB). The budget's purpose is to
stop bulk data reads, and these reads are not that. Since the 2026-11-03
rollout, the controller has written 32,251 objects totaling 90.5 GiB, or
20 to 32 GiB a day. That is far more than the 1 GB in-memory cache
holds, so any delivery or worker fetch more than about an hour after
submission reads from GCS. Workers keep their bundle store on local
disk, so this changes only controller-side reads.
- `_deliver_handoff` let that exception through, because it is neither a
`ConnectError` nor an `OSError`. The exception ended `_run_loop`, and
nothing restarts a per-peer thread. A failed delivery now stays pending
for the next pass, and the rest of its batch is still sent. A failed
loop step is now logged and retried; it no longer ends the thread.

This PR does not recover the live hub. A controller restart starts the
threads again and resets the budget, and the jobs still pending are
delivered on the next pass.

Fixes #11389. Incident records: [echo wiki
984](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/984) and
[982](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/982).

**Tests.** Two new tests in `test_federation_handoff.py`. Both fail on
`main`, and both pass with this change.
- In one batch, a handoff whose bundle read raises
`TransferBudgetExceeded` stays pending while the other handoff is
delivered. The pending one is delivered on the next pass.
- A sync pass that raises does not end the peer's sync thread.

The broad `except Exception` in `_deliver_handoff` has a cost: a handoff
that fails every time, because of a bug, is logged and retried on every
pass instead of failing. That is how `OSError` was already handled. A
narrower catch would let one bad handoff skip cancels and status sync
for its whole peer on every pass.

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

land in exception notes instead of replacing the primary failure.

Linux regressions cover argument overflow, diagnostic truncation, and
deletion failures during cancellation and cleanup.

The blocking-deletion and keep-alive behavior changes from the same
Atlas
branch depend on its provider-wait close path and stay there for now.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[iris] Admit 08a gVisor CPU work through a hostname-only TAS flavor (#11515)

gVisor CPU Pods on cw-us-east-08a could not be admitted by Kueue: the
CPU nodes lack the `ds.coreweave.com/nvlink.domain` key, and the only
TAS flavor, `cw-tas` bound to `multinode-nvlink-ib`, requires every
topology key to be present. CoreWeave's node metadata controller owns
the `backend.coreweave.cloud/*` labels and keeps them empty on CPU
nodes, so synthetic labels on the NodePool cannot fix this. Incident
record: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1007.

Each CoreWeave cluster now gets an `iris-cpu` ResourceFlavor selecting
its physical CPU pool by the Iris scale-group label, bound to a
hostname-only `iris-cpu-hostname` Topology: `cpu-erapids` on 08a,
`cpu-genoa` on 02a and `cpu-turin` on rno2a, set by
`provisioning.coreweave.kueue.cpu_scale_group`. It is first in
`iris-cq`'s resource group with zero GPU and RDMA quota, so CPU-only
PodSets prefer the CPU pool and can still spill to `cw-tas`; GPU and
RDMA work keeps the shared flavor and its binding quotas. The CPU pools'
NodePools stop declaring the four synthetic topology labels; capacity,
instance type and taints are unchanged. `build_cluster_queue` now orders
each flavor's resources by `coveredResources` instead of the caller's
mapping order.

Region constraints are now validated against the Kubernetes backend's
advertised region. The previous code emitted an `iris.region` node
selector that no CoreWeave Node carries (08a Nodes are labelled
`topology.kubernetes.io/region=US-EAST-08`, the backend advertises
`US-EAST-08A`). A required mismatch fails before Pod creation; preferred
regions do not restrict placement.

This PR changes no live infrastructure. The Kueue change takes effect
only through the per-cluster targeted Pulumi apply of four resources
(`topology-cpu`, `resource-flavor-cpu`, `cluster-queue`, and that
cluster's CPU NodePool), documented under "CPU topology admission" in
`lib/iris/OPS.md`, which needs separate explicit approval. The region
validation takes effect only after an Iris controller deployment.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[datakit] Isolate concurrent Bloom cache fills (#11565)

Concurrent cold-cache Bloom loads now use separate temporary directories
and atomically publish complete files to the node-local cache. Threads
in one process previously shared a PID-named partial file, allowing a
rename to remove another caller's source or a load to see truncated
data.

A synchronized four-thread reproduction failed with `FileNotFoundError`
before the change. It now loads the expected filter in every thread and
leaves cache bytes identical to the source.

Fixes #11564

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[levanter] Reuse final permanent checkpoints (#11552)

When the final hook follows a permanent save of the same step, wait for
that save and reuse it. This avoids a second TensorStore write into the
committed `step-N/` directory. The wait keeps pending save failures
ahead of later final hooks.

For a local 16 MiB checkpoint, the baseline forced save took 60 ms and
grew the directory from 16.8 to 33.6 MB; the revised path took less than
1 ms with no growth. A Trainer regression reproduces a failed second
manifest write on the baseline and restores the original checkpoint with
this change. Temporary final saves and restarts with a new Checkpointer
still rewrite the step path.

Part of #11534

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.message:
[evalrecords] Move evaluation records out of marin-core (#11477)

👨 why does Marina require rollout-engine, skyrl and trainer? it
transitively requires it via `marin-core` for some eval commons, this is
step 1 to reduce that dependency.

<hr>

🤖 
* move the evaluation run records, result readers, and statistics that
the Marina dashboards read out of `marin-core` into a new workspace
package, `marin-evalrecords` (`lib/evalrecords`); the evaldash and model
scorecard app code no longer imports `marin`
* step 1 of 2 toward a Marina image without `marin-core` [^1]
* the image listed the workspace closure of `marin-core` by hand, so
each new `marin-core` dependency broke the next image rebuild:
`rolloutengine` (#10966), then `skyrlrecipe`
([run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43576275701));
Marina uses neither
* this PR also copies `lib/skyrlrecipe` and `lib/evalrecords` into the
image, which repairs the Marina rollout that is red on main; replaces
#11474
* `evalrecords` must not import `marin` or the code that runs
evaluations [^2]
* moved from `marin.evaluation`: `records`, `eval_stats`,
`eval_measurements`, `eval_policy`, `eval_policy_sources`,
`metric_selection`, `historical_protocols`, `model_identity`,
`repeat_aggregates`, `lm_eval_samples`
  * `marin.rollouts.evaluation_results` → `evalrecords.rollout_results`
* `marin.rollouts.evaluation` keeps the runner; the stored models
(`Attempt`, `AttemptPhase`, `ATTEMPTS_TABLE`, `RUN_OBJECT`) move to
`evalrecords.rollout_attempts`
* `eval_task_directory` moves to `evalrecords.records`, so the sample
readers do not import `levanter`
* the `STATUS_*` constants and a status reader, `read_step_status`, move
to `rigging.filesystem.step_status`; `StatusFile` and the step lock stay
in `marin.execution.step_status` [^3]
* all call sites import from the new locations; no compatibility shims
* three evaldash test modules build their fixtures from `evalrecords`
and finestore types; `test_curated.py` still drives the evaluation
runner and imports `marin`
* `marin-evalrecords` joins the Python library release family, because
the published `marin-core` wheel depends on it [^4]

[^1]: released app revisions live in Postgres and still import `marin`,
so the image keeps `marin-core` until evaldash and the model scorecard
are released from this commit. Step 2 then removes `marin-core` from
Marina; a local build of that image is 1.73 GB against 3.38 GB, with 183
locked third-party packages against 266. A rollback to an app revision
from before this PR will not work after step 2.
[^2]: the `evalrecords` test scope runs `lib/evalrecords/tests` in an
environment with only the package's declared dependencies, and a test
there imports every module, so an import of `marin` or a training
library fails. Only the statistics tests moved; the tests that also need
`marin` stay under `tests/`.
[^3]: open question: `rigging` now owns the path, tokens, and reader of
the executor's `.executor_status` file. The dashboards read that file,
so the reader must sit below `marin-core`.
[^4]: needs a `marin-evalrecords` project with a trusted publisher on
PyPI before this PR merges: the release workflow publishes the library
family on each push to `main` that changes `lib/evalrecords/src`.

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
[ops] Post Iris jobs active for more than a week to Slack (#11139)

Add a weekday Loom watch, `old-iris-jobs`, that posts Iris root jobs
active for more than 7 days to `#marin-alerts`. Each line gives the
cluster that runs the job, the job, owner, age, and the CPU, memory,
disk, and device of the job's active tasks. Jobs that hold a GPU or TPU
come first, then the oldest jobs. The message's cancel command names the
`marin` hub, which routes a cancel to the CoreWeave peer that runs a
federated job, so owners do not need CoreWeave port-forward access. The
watch runs `scripts/ops/old_iris_jobs.py` against the hub, posts the
messages it writes, and keeps its state in the Loom watch state.

A job is posted once while its root job keeps running. A preempted task
returns to pending while its job stays running, so a job whose tasks all
wait keeps its place in the state and is not posted again when it
resumes. A job that stops running leaves the state and is posted again
if it becomes old and active later. Child jobs count toward their root,
because the owner cancels the root. Loom rejects posts above 4,000 bytes
and cannot attach a file, so the script splits the report into messages
of at most 3,500 bytes and the watch posts them all in one run. If a
post is not confirmed, the watch leaves the state unchanged and the next
run posts the report again.

On 2026-11-16 the hub had 80 such root jobs, 78 with an active task and
21 with a GPU or TPU. A read-only run of the script against the hub,
starting from empty state, wrote 4 messages with all 78 jobs; a second
run with the new state wrote none.

Jobs submitted directly to a CoreWeave controller are not in the report,
because Loom has no CoreWeave kubeconfig. The hub mirrors the jobs it
federates, so those are covered; an operator can run the script with
`--cluster <cw-cluster>` and a separate state file. The watch does not
cancel jobs; the [cancellation
decision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11113#issuecomment-6754759823)
is to report only for 4 weeks first.

Fixes #11113
